name: Eli Arnold

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Arnold lists his occupation as bicycle cop.
Arnold's pamphlet statement lists a BS from Portland State University and training at the Military Intelligence Center and Oregon DPSST.
bio.excerpt: Portland State University, BS; Military Intelligence Center, Oregon Dept. Public Safety Standards and Training

bio.statement: Arnold's pamphlet statement lists experience as a Multnomah County Democrats precinct committee person, U.S. Army Blackhawk pilot and intelligence analyst, and 2016 Bernie Sanders delegate.
bio.excerpt: Multnomah County Democrats PCP, U.S. Army Blackhawk Pilot & Intelligence Analyst, 2016 Bernie Sanders Delegate

bio.statement: OPB reports Arnold is a Portland police officer who narrowly lost a District 4 race in 2024.
bio.excerpt: a Portland police officer who narrowly lost a District 4 seat in the 2024 election

bio.statement: OPB reports Arnold, as a downtown bike officer, has focused on high-volume fentanyl dealers and changing drug laws.
bio.excerpt: As a bike cop in downtown Portland, Arnold has spent much of his time focused on cracking down on high-volume fentanyl dealers and navigating ever-changing drug laws.

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Arnold says the city should cut bureaucracy, get people into homes and move people from tents to shelter and services.
positions.excerpt: Let's cut the bureaucracy, get people into homes, and move people from tents to shelter and services.

positions.statement: Arnold's pamphlet statement says he will prioritize staffing and coordination across police, fire, dispatch and behavioral health response.
positions.excerpt: I'll prioritize staffing and coordination across police, fire, dispatch, and behavioral health response

positions.statement: Arnold's pamphlet statement supports using existing clean energy resources to move toward fareless transit.
positions.excerpt: I support using existing clean energy resources to move toward fareless transit,

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Arnold says he will not support raising taxes and fees.
positions.excerpt: I will not support raising taxes and fees.

positions.statement: Arnold's pamphlet statement says he will push for accountability by measuring outcomes and reporting results.
positions.excerpt: I'll push for accountability—measuring outcomes, reporting results, and ensuring every dollar delivers real value.

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 12 District 4 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form (linked from portland.gov 2026 city candidates page); (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the two articles that profile every District 4 candidate: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 4 council race' (2026-10-07) and Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 4' (2026-09-11). Multi-winner race: OPB states three District 4 seats are on the ballot. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Filing form gives occupation 'Police Officer'.
